# Belinda

## Overview

- **Age:** Fourteen years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Role:** Domestic servant and handmaiden for Miss Rosalind Penrose  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- **Titles:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Appearance

She wears extremely blue bows. Her physical appearance closely mirrors that of her older sisters (the former Charlottas).

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P47](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0047)_

## Personality

Belinda is a practical, honest, and fiercely loyal young servant. Unlike her sisters, she refrains from criticizing Miss Rosalind's imaginative nature and takes deep pride in caring for her mistress. She admits to having little tolerance for men and frequently worries about her own tendency to break household crockery.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)_

## Traits

- Loyal and devoted  <sub>[v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- Clumsy with crockery  <sub>[v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- Dislikes men  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
- Dislikes Boston  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Abilities

- Baking and food preparation  <sub>[v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056)</sub>
- Playing the horn to produce echoes  <sub>[v2 c21 P70](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0070), [v2 c21 P71](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0071)</sub>

## Goals

- Imitate Nell Harcourt's speech, posture, and walking style  <sub>[v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039)</sub>
- Ensure Miss Rosalind is well cared for and happy  <sub>[v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>

## History

Born as Leonora Bowman, she went to live with Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage in exchange for room, board, and clothes, succeeding her older sisters Belinda (Belinda the First), Julietta (Belinda the Second), and Evelina (Belinda the Third). Because of her sisters' resemblance, Miss Rosalind called her 'Belinda the Fourth' to avoid confusion. Unlike her elder sisters, Belinda never mocked Miss Rosalind's imaginative pretending and served as her dedicated helper, despite her tendency to let tea boil or accidentally shatter dishes. During a visit by Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke, Belinda assisted with serving tea and demonstrated the estate's famous echoes by sounding a tin horn and chuckling for the visitors. As she approached her teenage years, she privately attempted to practice walking and speaking like Nell, whom she idolized. Recognizing signs of illness and loneliness in Miss Rosalind after a winter walk, Belinda confided her deep worries to Nell. Later, when Stephen Stanhope's visit was arranged, she confronted Nell to learn the secret and voiced her earnest hope that Stephen would marry Miss Rosalind so her mistress would be looked after when Belinda reached sixteen and had to move to Boston.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c21 P70](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0070), [v2 c21 P71](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0071), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)_

## Background by volume

- Her actual birth name is Leonora Bowman  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- She is the youngest and finest of the Bowman daughters  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- She came to work at Echo Cottage following her three older sisters, who all departed for Boston upon turning sixteen  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> However, I would prefer looking like you to being attractive  <sub>[v2 c27 P40](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0040)</sub>

> Please, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, it can easily be noticed that a secret exists between you and Miss Rosalind, and I believe, asking for your forgiveness if I am being overly bold, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, that withholding it from me is truly unkind, considering how close we have all been as friends.  <sub>[v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048)</sub>

> It’s my hope he weds Miss Rosalind. Certain women are meant to be spinsters right from the beginning, and I fear I belong to that group, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, on account of having precious little tolerance for men. Miss Rosalind, however, never was meant for that. I’ve been dreadfully anxious, pondering whatever would become of her once I grew so large that I must depart for Boston. No other girls remain in our family, and heaven only knows what would happen to her if she hired a stranger who could mock her imaginative play, leave items scattered out of place, and refuse to accept the name Belinda the Fifth. She could find a person who wouldn’t prove as unfortunate as I am at smashing crockery, but she’ll never find a single person who’d cherish her more.  <sub>[v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>
